## Proposal and provenance

Stable algorithm slug: `merge-probability-provenance`. Source: pm-4k6b note recorded 2026-07-25T12:33:09.924Z.

Planning pass 2026-07-25 (directed maintainer pass): Algorithm (20) merge-probability-weighted provenance ranking — in a fleet working on branches, a workspace read on one branch sees facts of three kinds: mainline facts, this branch's own uncommitted facts, and facts that exist only in sibling branches once federation or merge preview makes them visible. Ranking them equally is wrong in both directions: an agent that trusts a sibling branch's not-yet-merged decision may build on work that never lands, while an agent that ignores its own branch's fresh decisions re-derives what it just decided. Mechanism: attach to each candidate fact a provenance weight derived from its position relative to the merge frontier — mainline facts weight 1, own-branch facts weight 1 for the authoring agent and decay for others, sibling-branch facts weight by an estimated merge probability. The estimate needs no prediction model: the history stream already carries the base rates that matter — how often branches by this author on this item class merge, how long the branch has diverged, whether it touches items already closed on mainline. Score contribution stays linear so the explanation surface can say a candidate was demoted because it exists only on an unmerged branch, which is the kind of explanation an agent can act on. Degenerate correctly: single-branch workspaces see weight 1 everywhere and identical behaviour to today. Relation: this is a signal feeding the (3) linear combination, not a new stage; it depends on merge-frontier visibility, so it is only actionable once cross-branch reads exist (pm-odohgb, pm-76dnfg).

## Delivery boundary

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented.

## Experiment protocol

Freeze a workspace/history revision and parameter manifest. Compare against the current deterministic SDK baseline using held-out judgments and negative controls. Report nDCG/action success, critical-evidence omission, latency p50/p95, peak memory, tokens per completed task, and rebuild cost separately. Include 3-item/minutes, real-shaped, 100k/1M-item, decades-long, and sparse/dense/imbalanced graph scenarios; smoke subsets may not claim scale acceptance. Bound candidate counts, graph expansions, elapsed time, and output size, with cancellation and completeness receipts. Record exact versus approximate behavior and approximation error; theoretical guarantees require their stated assumptions. Missing or untrusted evidence remains unknown, never inferred proof.

Promotion requires a reproducible quality improvement on the held-out target population, no regression of existing exact invariants or mandatory gates, and a declared compute/token cost justified by that improvement. Reject or defer with the same immutable evidence if those conditions fail. No production default, adaptive learning, or data export is authorized by this planning item.
